title: Sunrise GPU warmup + quick ops todo
body:
Purpose:
Quick personal checklist for the early shift — minimal handoff, get GPUs hot, verify networking, and leave notes for midday. Kept intentionally terse so I can run through it on the rack.

Context/notes to self:
- Today: expected spike from a customer test at 09:30 PT (approx 50k tokens over 15m). Want to pre-warm ~30% of fleet to avoid cold-cache tail latencies.
- Priority: avoid ephemeral OOMs and long compilation stalls. If anything looks off, route traffic to dedicated-nonpreempt region (eu-west-2-dedicated) and notify SRE on #infra-ops.

Warmup plan (order matters):
1) Node selection (~05:15)
   - Query current queue length: curl -s http://fleet-api.local/queues | jq '.total_pending' 
   - Pick nodes with oldest idle_time < 6h and GPU temp < 45C (prefer same AZ as expected region).
   - Target: 12 nodes on p8d equivalent (or mix) to cover 30% burst.

2) Container spin-up (~05:20)
   - kubectl -n inference scale deploy/gpu-worker --replicas=12 --record
   - Monitor pod readiness: kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-worker -w (stop when 12 are Ready)

3) Model cache warm (~05:35)
   - For each selected node: ssh jump -> sudo systemctl start gpu-cache-loader@model-x
   - Check /var/log/gpu-cache-loader.log for progress; expect 1–2min per model depending on quantized size.

4) KV/prefix validation (~05:45)
   - Run small synthetic batch: python tools/send_warm_request.py --model model-x --batch 8 --tokens 128
   - Verify latency P95 < 120ms and no KV cache misses. If miss rate > 5% re-run loader.

Networking checks (quick):
- iperf3 between node and redis-proxy (10.0.2.x) — 1 check per AZ.
- traceroute to model-repo S3 endpoint (s3-us-west-2) to confirm no packet-loss.
- If packet drop > 1% escalate to neteng with trace and timestamp.

Quick ops TODOs / reminders:
- Rotate token for backup-sync task (cron @ 06:00). Reminder: renew KMS key alias before midnight. Ticket JIRA-OPS-4821 tracks this.
- Check dmesg for nv_peer_mem or driver warnings: sudo dmesg | grep -i nvidia | tail -n 40
- Confirm NTP drift < 1s: chronyc tracking || date && sudo chronyc makestep if offset > 0.5s
- Zpool health on /var/lib/models: sudo zpool status -v (watch for read errors)

If things go south (escalation play):
- Symptom: compilation freeze (>2 min per init)
   - Action: kill init on offending node, drain, and re-schedule: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data; kubectl uncordon when fixed.
   - Fallback: switch traffic via routing-policy tag: policy=warmup-fallback -> route to hosted-capacity-2

Handoff notes to midday (put on ticket and slack snippet):
- Warmup completed at 05:52 (12 nodes). KV misses initially 12% -> reloaded model-x on 3 nodes -> stabilized to 1.6%
- Observed short-term P95 spike to 300ms during model load window; no customer errors reported.
- Left pre-warm group under tag: warmup-20260313-A (so console rollbacks are easier).

Loose questions / follow-ups:
- Can we automate the KV warm verification step as a pre-deploy gate? (cc @Marcus)
- Consider a low-cost persistent cache tier on local NVMe to reduce reload times for big quantized models. Explore with research team.

Personal notes / reminders: 
- Bring spare USB-C cable to rack (lost last one)
- Send short note to Diego with the loader script timings (attach logs)

Timestamps (for when I run):
- 05:12 start checklist
- 05:18 scale -> pods creating
- 05:30 cache loaders kicked off
- 05:52 all nodes ready, verification run green

---
Raw commands I ran (paste for ticket):
- curl -s http://fleet-api.local/queues | jq '.total_pending'
- kubectl -n inference scale deploy/gpu-worker --replicas=12 --record
- kubectl get pods -l app=gpu-worker -w
- sudo systemctl start gpu-cache-loader@model-x
- python tools/send_warm_request.py --model model-x --batch 8 --tokens 128
- sudo dmesg | grep -i nvidia | tail -n 40

End of scratchpad — will tidy into proper postmortem if anything anomalous shows up during the customer test.
